Open it and confirm it shows what was claimed

questions.intro: AI answers often include LINKS and DATED FACTS that may no longer work or be true. A link can be BROKEN (the page moved or was deleted), lead to the WRONG PAGE, or be completely made up. A fact can be STALE: a price, rule, schedule or contact that has changed. Before sharing or relying on a link, open it and confirm it shows what the answer claims. Before relying on a dated fact, find a current source. Pay special attention to phone numbers and email addresses, since a wrong one can send you to the wrong organization or even a scammer.

sections.skill: Avoid look-alike links and stale cached pages

questions.prompt: An answer links to "paypa1-support.example." What should you notice?

choices.text: It is a misspelled look-alike address
Nothing, because a small spelling difference in a web address never changes where it goes
It must be the official site
All support sites look like this

questions.correct_answer: It is a misspelled look-alike address
questions.intro: Look-alike links are a risk: a slightly misspelled website address can belong to someone else entirely. When you need an organization's page, reach it through a source you trust, such as typing its known address or using a search engine, rather than clicking an unverified link. Old cached pages and archived copies can also look current. Check a page's date and look for "last updated" notes, and for official matters, use the organization's main site.
